title: Republic of Indonesia
capsule: The Republic of Indonesia declared independence on 17 August 1945 under Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta, days after Japan's surrender, and consolidated its sovereignty through the Indonesian National Revolution, ending with the Dutch transfer of sovereignty in December 1949. Sukarno's 'Guided Democracy' (1959–1965) centralized power and pursued a non-aligned foreign policy, while the 1965 coup attempt and Suharto's subsequent seizure of power inaugurated the 'New Order' authoritarian regime that lasted until 1998. After Suharto's resignation amid the Asian financial crisis, Indonesia transitioned to multi-party democracy; today it is the world's fourth most populous country and the largest archipelagic state, spanning over 17,000 islands.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. National territory is defined by a series of Dutch colonial boundary agreements and the 1949 sovereignty transfer; offshore boundaries with neighbors such as Malaysia, Timor-Leste, and Papua New Guinea are defined by treaties of varying completion, with some maritime zones still under negotiation.
